title: Postmortem: Control plane routing blackhole in private/VPC during canary control-plane upgrade
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a canary upgrade of the private control-plane in a customer VPC, a subset of control-plane replicas lost network reachability from worker nodes and health probes. The outage lasted ~42 minutes for affected clusters and caused API request failures, job scheduling delays, and degraded control-plane metrics for three customers on Dedicated Private deployments. Initial mitigation was a canary rollback and emergency route reprogramming. Impact: high (customers experienced 5xx API errors and inability to create new pods).
timeline:
2026-03-01T10:05Z - Upgrade started for control-plane canary group on customer-vpc-29
2026-03-01T10:22Z - Automated health probes from workers began failing to reach the new canary control-plane replicas; alerts triggered
2026-03-01T10:28Z - Canary was paused by on-call engineer after cross-region worker nodes reported API timeouts
2026-03-01T10:33Z - Attempted rolling back canary failed to restore connectivity due to asymmetric routing on the upgrade hosts
2026-03-01T10:45Z - Manual remediation: reprogrammed ENI route table entries and applied iptables rule correction on two upgrade hosts
2026-03-01T10:47Z - Control-plane connectivity restored for most nodes; follow-up verification and long-tail errors resolved by 11:00Z
root_cause_summary: A control-plane package in the canary included an updated networking component (CNI-related helper binary) that reordered iptables/nft rules when applied. On some private upgrade hosts this resulted in insertion of a DNAT rule that inadvertently superseded the management port SNAT/DNAT used by cross-subnet worker->control-plane traffic. In combination with a kernel route metric change (caused by a system package bump in the same image), traffic took an asymmetric path through a NAT device that did not have the expected DNAT entries, creating a routing blackhole for the control-plane management port. The change slipped through because our pre-upgrade e2e network regression tests did not cover the specific iptables rule ordering interaction across Ubuntu kernels used by a subset of customer images.
mitigations_taken: 1) Immediate: Paused canary and prevented further rollouts to other VPCs. 2) Rolled back control-plane package for canary instances where rollback succeeded. 3) For hosts where rollback could not restore state quickly, manually reprogrammed ENI route tables and corrected iptables rule ordering via an emergency orchestrated script. 4) Added temporary pod-level retry/backoff rules to reduce 5xx propagation to customers. 5) Notified affected customers and offered post-incident support.
action_items: ENG-11421: Add a pre-upgrade networking regression test that validates iptables/nft rule ordering across supported kernel versions (owner: Jing Wei, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-11422: Harden canary rollout pipeline to block upgrades that change iptables/nft rules or kernel networking modules without explicit safety flags (owner: Marco Diaz, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-11423: Build an automated ENI/route-table sanity check in private upgrade playbooks to detect asymmetric routing post-upgrade (owner: Oliver Thompson, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-21)
ENG-11424: Update runbooks and incident run play to include immediate route-table and iptables validation steps for private/VPC upgrades (owner: Aisha Patel, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-10)

ENG-11425: Create a post-deployment traffic probe from worker-subnet to control-plane-subnet for 5s at 1m intervals for the first 30 minutes after upgrade (owner: SRE Team, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-17)
ENG-11426: Add telemetry to detect sudden changes in kernel route metrics and correlate with package upgrades (owner: Research/Infra, estimate: 5, due: 2026-04-01)
PM-578: Communicate a clarified private deployment upgrade policy and optional pre-upgrade test engagement for customers with custom kernel images (owner: Maya Rivera, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-12)
